messages:
maria_sales: Quick heads-up — AcmeCorp POC. They want a Dedicated pool but all outbound traffic originates from their corp network behind a mandatory web proxy/NAT. They need to allowlist our egress, but their security team only gives static IPs for a limited window. how do we want to handle?

dan_engineer: do they have a list of static egress IPs or ranges? if they can only provide temporary ones we can coordinate timeboxed access. otherwise we can offer our static-egress add-on for Dedicated.

ryan_se: two trenches: 1) provide Redwood static egress IPs (Dedicated add-on) and they allowlist those; 2) customer sets up a TLS/SSH tunnel/bastion to route traffic — increases complexity but avoids them needing to change firewall rules.

maria_sales: they said "we can't change prod fw rules, only allow temporary IPs for vendor POCs" — suggests they can't take on a permanent add-on. price sensitivity too.

evansre: note: if they route via a customer bastion+SNAT we need to ensure our Dedicated endpoint accepts requests with original source preserved for quotas/rate-limits. otherwise rate limiting may be per-bastion. also watch timeouts for long-running streams.

ryan_se: good call. options/quick tradeoffs I gave them earlier: 
- Static egress (redwood-managed): simplest for them, we give up-to 3 IPs, costs as an Enterprise add-on.
- Timeboxed allowlist: they provide a 2-4 hour window and list of IPs, we schedule a maintenance window and smoke tests. low cost but brittle.
- Bastion/proxy (customer-managed): we accept traffic from their bastion IPs; preserves no extra billing but requires customer infra work and TLS termination rules.
- VPN / Private VPC peering: full private connectivity, longer setup, fits Private product.

maria_sales: can you paste the snippet for what to ask their infra team?

dan_engineer: sure — paste this to them:

```
Please confirm:
1) Exact source IPv4/IPv6 addresses or CIDR ranges you will NAT outbound from for the POC (e.g. 198.51.100.0/24).
2) Time windows (UTC) we can expect those IPs to be in use.
3) Whether your corporate proxy performs TLS interception (MITM) or allows passthrough for vendor TLS.
4) If you can run an SSH bastion, what IP(s) would be used and do you allow port 443/8443 outbound to our endpoints.
5) Contact for on-call during the POC and expected SLA for rule changes.
```

ryan_se: also add: if they want token-scoped access we can issue one-time API keys for the POC and revoke after. useful for security reviews.

maria_sales: pricing question — what's ballpark for the static-egress add-on on a month POC?

evan_sre: ping @infra_bot to open a ticket for pricing/ops quote.

infra_bot: created ticket #OPS-4821 for static-egress pricing / Dedicated pool nuance, assigned to @ryan_se. ETA 2 business days. :white_check_mark:

ryan_se: replied in OPS-4821 — estimate for timeboxed POC support (manual scheduling + on-call) is no additional charge for first 8 hours. static egress add-on pricing is handled by sales; will provide range in ticket.

maria_sales: great. i'll send the reqs to Acme infra and ask for a 4-hour window to start. i'll include the code snippet and ask them to confirm TLS interception behavior. will update thread when they respond. :+1:

dan_engineer: one more gotcha — if their proxy rewrites headers we may see mismatched client IPs in logs. flag it for them to preserve X-Forwarded-For if possible.

maria_sales: noted, i'll add that to the email. thanks everyone.
